I need to identify the molecular formula of a compound in a sample. The only tool available is mass spectrometry with ESI (Electrospray Ionization) technique. 

Mass spectrometry will give me mass-to-charge (m/z) ratios of ions, which can help determine the molecular weight of the compound. From the molecular weight and the fragmentation pattern, I can deduce the molecular formula.

Let me start by obtaining the mass spectrometry data.

<thought>
The mass spectrometry data shows:
- Base peak at m/z 127.09971 (100% intensity)
- Isotope peak at m/z 128.10284 (8.12% intensity)
- Additional smaller isotope peaks at m/z 129, 130, 131, 132

The base peak at m/z 127.09971 likely represents [M+H]+ (protonated molecular ion) in ESI positive mode, which is common for ESI-MS.

If m/z 127.09971 is [M+H]+, then the molecular weight M = 127.09971 - 1.00783 = 126.09188

Now I need to determine what molecular formula gives a mass of approximately 126.09188.

Let me consider common elements and their masses:
- C: 12.000
- H: 1.008
- N: 14.003
- O: 15.999

The isotope pattern can help confirm:
- The M+1 peak is about 8.12% of the base peak
- For carbon, each C contributes about 1.1% to M+1
- 8.12% / 1.1% ≈ 7.4, suggesting around 7-8 carbons

Let me try different combinations for mass ≈ 126.09:

C7H9NO (7×12 + 9×1.008 + 14.003 + 15.999 = 84 + 9.072 + 14.003 + 15.999 = 123.074) - too low

C7H10N2 (7×12 + 10×1.008 + 2×14.003 = 84 + 10.08 + 28.006 = 122.086) - too low

C6H9NO2 (6×12 + 9×1.008 + 14.003 + 2×15.999 = 72 + 9.072 + 14.003 + 31.998 = 127.073) - close but slightly low

C7H13NO (7×12 + 13×1.008 + 14.003 + 15.999 = 84 + 13.104 + 14.003 + 15.999 = 127.106) - very close!

Let me verify C7H13NO more precisely:
C7H13NO = 7×12.000 + 13×1.00783 + 14.00307 + 15.99491 = 84.000 + 13.10179 + 14.00307 + 15.99491 = 127.09977

This matches almost exactly with 127.09971!

The molecular formula is C7H13NO.
</thought>
